#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/common.sh"

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
Usage: beacon-status [--file FILE] [--stale-minutes N] [--quiet]

Check every beacon in the status file and print one line each:

  OK     lamp lit, heard from recently, battery healthy
  WARN   stale (no report for N minutes) or battery below 20%
  FAIL   lamp reported anything other than "ok"

Options:
  --file FILE         status file (default: \$BEACON_STATUS_FILE or data/status.txt)
  --stale-minutes N   minutes of silence before a beacon is stale (default: 30)
  --quiet             print only beacons that are not OK
  -h, --help          show this help

Exit status: 0 all OK, 1 any WARN, 2 any FAIL, 64 usage error.
USAGE
}

file="${BEACON_STATUS_FILE}"
stale_minutes=30
quiet=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --file) file="${2:?--file needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --stale-minutes) stale_minutes="${2:?--stale-minutes needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --quiet) quiet=true; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) usage >&2; exit 64 ;;
    esac
done

[[ "${stale_minutes}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "--stale-minutes must be a whole number"

require_status "${file}"
now="$(now_epoch)"
worst=0

while IFS='|' read -r id name lamp last_seen battery; do
    state=OK
    notes=()
    if [[ "${lamp}" != "ok" ]]; then
        state=FAIL
        notes+=("lamp ${lamp}")
    fi
    seen="$(iso_to_epoch "${last_seen}")"
    age=$(( (now - seen) / 60 ))
    if (( age > stale_minutes )); then
        [[ "${state}" == FAIL ]] || state=WARN
        notes+=("silent ${age}m")
    fi
    if [[ "${battery}" < 20 ]]; then
        [[ "${state}" == FAIL ]] || state=WARN
        notes+=("battery ${battery}%")
    fi

    case "${state}" in
        WARN) (( worst < 1 )) && worst=1 ;;
        FAIL) worst=2 ;;
    esac

    if [[ "${quiet}" == true && "${state}" == OK ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    printf '%-4s  %-6s %-18s %s\n' "${state}" "${id}" "${name}" "${notes[*]:-}"
done < <(read_status "${file}")

exit "${worst}"
# id|name|lamp|last_seen (UTC)|battery %
BX01|Carrick Point|ok|2026-10-07T05:52:00Z|87
BX02|Skellan Rock|ok|2026-10-07T05:49:00Z|100
BX03|Porthwenna Head|dim|2026-10-07T05:51:00Z|64
BX04|Saltmere Ness|ok|2026-10-07T03:10:00Z|41
BX05|Dunvarrow Light|ok|2026-10-07T05:55:00Z|9

@@ -4,7 +4,7 @@ source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/common.sh"

-Usage: beacon-report [--file FILE] [--date YYYY-MM-DD]
+Usage: beacon-report [--file FILE] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--conditions FILE]
 
 Print the daily report for the lighthouse network: a count of beacons by
 state, every beacon that needs a visit, and the fleet's average battery.
@@ -12,23 +12,29 @@ state, every beacon that needs a visit, and the fleet's average battery.
 Options:
   --file FILE   status file (default: \$BEACON_STATUS_FILE or data/status.txt)
   --date DATE   date printed in the header (default: today, UTC)
+  --conditions FILE
+                print a Conditions: line per station in FILE, whose lines

   -h, --help    show this help

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
Usage: test/run.sh [--help] [PATTERN]

Run every test_* function in this file whose name matches PATTERN
(default: all). Each test runs in its own subshell and scratch directory.
USAGE
}

[[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]] && { usage; exit 0; }
pattern="${1:-}"

HERE="$(cd -- "$(dirname "$0")" >/dev/null && pwd)"

    [[ "$1" == "$2" ]] || fail "expected [$2], got [$1]"
}

assert_contains() {
    [[ "$1" == *"$2"* ]] || fail "expected output to contain [$2], got:"$'\n'"$1"
}

assert_file() {
    [[ -e "$1" ]] || fail "expected $1 to exist"
}

assert_no_file() {
    [[ ! -e "$1" ]] || fail "expected $1 not to exist"
}

    echo "${code}"
}

}

test_status_when_a_lamp_is_not_ok_it_should_exit_2() {
    assert_eq "$(status_exit --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt")" 2
}

test_status_when_a_lamp_is_dim_it_should_mark_it_failed() {

}

test_status_when_a_beacon_is_silent_it_should_warn_with_the_age() {

}

test_status_when_the_battery_is_low_it_should_warn() {

}

test_status_when_the_stale_window_is_widened_it_should_not_warn() {

    out="$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" --stale-minutes 180 || true)"
    [[ "${out}" != *"silent"* ]] || fail "still reported silent beacons"
}

test_status_when_quiet_it_should_omit_ok_beacons() {
    local out
    out="$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" --quiet || true)"

}

test_status_when_the_file_is_missing_it_should_exit_64() {
    assert_eq "$(status_exit --file "${SCRATCH}/nope.txt")" 64
}

input.body: Cause: bin/beacon-status checked low battery with `[[ "${battery}" < 20 ]]`, which is a string (lexicographic) comparison. "100" sorts before "20", so a full battery gave WARN. "9" sorts after "20", so a nearly flat battery gave OK. Fix: use an arithmetic comparison, `(( 10#${battery} < 20 ))`; the 10# prefix also keeps a zero-padded value from being read as octal. Added tests in test/run.sh for a 100% battery (no warning) and a 9% battery (warns). All 22 tests pass. Against data/status.txt, Skellan Rock is now OK and Dunvarrow Light is WARN (battery 9%).

BCN-207 is fixed, commented on and closed. I didn't commit anything. All 22 tests in `test/run.sh` pass.

- **Cause:** `bin/beacon-status` compared battery levels with `[[ "${battery}" < 20 ]]`, which compares them as text. "100" sorts before "20", so Skellan Rock got a WARN. "9" sorts after "20", so Dunvarrow Light was reported OK.
- **Reproduction:** against `data/status.txt` it showed exactly what the issue described.
- **Fix:** the check is now `(( 10#${battery} < 20 ))`, a numeric comparison. Against `data/status.txt`, Skellan Rock is now OK and Dunvarrow Light is WARN (battery 9%).
- **Tests:** I added one test for a 100% battery (no warning) and one for a 9% battery (warns). They use a new fixture, `test/fixtures/battery.txt`.

The comment on BCN-207 gives the cause and the fix.

Your uncommitted `beacon-report` and `conditions` changes were already in the working tree and I left them alone.
